prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Katy, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1294; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Nothing independent confirms the accident: no witnesses, no photos and no other report.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was stopped in the right lane of the frontbound feeder road near Katy, Texas, when the vehicle behind them, operated by Driver 2, struck the rear bumper. Driver 1 advised that the impact pushed their vehicle forward a short distance before it came to rest. A Passenger was also in the vehicle, though the Passenger's exact seating position at the moment of impact could not be fully established during the interview. Driver 1 reported low back pain and stiffness and was offered medical evaluation at the scene, which was declined at that time. Damage to the rear of Driver 1's vehicle is consistent with the reported impact, and no prior damage to the vehicle was known to Driver 1 or observed by the responding officer. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy involved. No independent witnesses were located, no photographs of the scene were provided, and no other crash report was on file for the location at the time of this review. Driver 2 was cited for following too closely.
